cases.name: cold-implementation-retains-intent
cases.prompt: Prepare a compact handoff for a web review queue. Accepted intent: calm oversight, retain item identity through review and return, urgent corrections before general activity. The real project has ui/queue.html, ui/tokens.css, and docs/patterns/review-return.md; all are current. An accepted exception lets long reviewer names wrap. A static prototype informed density but did not exercise keyboard behavior. Describe the handoff inline, without writing files or claiming to inspect the files.
cases.trap: An implementation-ready handoff names components but loses character, accepted exceptions, and evidence limitations.
expectations: Carries concrete character and craft criteria inside the existing handoff, not a separate authority hierarchy.
References the supplied real patterns for downstream inspection and describes how the review/return journey must compose.
Distinguishes the wrapping exception from general defaults and identifies unresolved/material keyboard observations.
Keeps static-prototype evidence bounded and does not claim it proves production interaction.
negative_expectations: Do not invent file contents or claim references were inspected.
Do not require a new brand approval or present prototype behavior as established production proof.

cases.name: small-handoff-stays-small
cases.prompt: The accepted settings design already defines the interaction, keyboard behavior, and product direction. We are only clarifying one field's empty-state help text to say which format is accepted. Give the smallest useful design handoff, inline.
cases.trap: The expanded handoff shape becomes a mandatory branding and documentation quota.
expectations: Inherits the accepted design and limits the handoff to the relevant copy change and its intent.
States a concrete check of the new help text without inventing a product-wide direction.
negative_expectations: Do not mandate new personas, alternative layouts, brand documents, or additional approval stages.
